data.source_title: 2025 National Guidelines for a Behavioral Health Coordinated System of Crisis Care
data.locator: Executive Summary / “Essential Elements of a Crisis System”; system elements “Someone to Contact,” “Someone to Respond,” and “A Safe Place for Help”
data.source_setting: U.S. community behavioral-health crisis systems, including crisis lines, mobile crisis response, and stabilization settings; not an ED-specific clinical decision algorithm.
value: Connect people in crisis to immediate contact support (e.g., 988 or another behavioral-health hotline).
Dispatch mobile crisis response based on assessed need, with de-escalation and connection to care.
Route to an appropriate safe stabilization setting for immediate treatment/support, with crisis-system coordination.
data.source_evidence_basis: SAMHSA 2025 national guidance names three foundational system elements: someone to contact, someone to respond, and a safe place for help; it describes hotline/988, mobile crisis teams, and stabilization services respectively.
data.limitations: Community system design guidance, not a patient-level suicide-risk assessment, involuntary-hold rule, or ED disposition protocol. Actual service availability and escalation criteria vary by jurisdiction.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent crisis presentation as a safety and needs assessment followed by locally available contact/response/stabilization options; urgent medical needs and immediate safety concerns require human clinician judgment and local emergency procedures.
data.applicability: Behavioral-health emergency/crisis system planning in the U.S.; local service map and legal requirements determine operational routing.
data.source_period: 2025 national guideline; SAMHSA resource page lists publication date 2025-01-15. No patient cohort period applies.
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
